Aliases_in_paper: P. falciparum apicoplast calcium binding protein 1

GeneSummary.bullet_point: MAL13P1.156 is a 64 kDa protein containing an EF-hand domain (prediction e-value 2.80E-13) positioned between amino acids 234-518, with a signal anchor probability of 0.954 and 5 of 5 positive tests for apicoplast targeting peptide at its C-terminus.
supporting_quotes: MAL13P1.156 is a single exon gene (1599 bp) that codes for a 64 kDa protein and contains an EF-hand domain (prediction e-value, 2.80E −13) at the position between 234 and 518 amino acid of the deduced polypeptide
identified MAL13P1.156, a calcium binding protein that contain a signal anchor with probability of 0.954 and 5 of 5 positive tests for an apicoplast targeting peptide at its C-terminus

GeneSummary.bullet_point: The protein localizes to the apicoplast, showing characteristic single small compartment in early schizonts, elongated branched formation in late schizonts, and divided punctuate formations in daughter merozoites, with partial colocalization with apicoplast marker EF-Tu.
supporting_quotes: immunofluorescence microscopy (IFA) of the transgenic cell line using the anti-GFP antibody shows the characteristic pattern of apicoplast localization with a single small compartment in the early schizonts, elongated branched formation in the late schizonts, and finally divided punctuate formations corresponding to new apicoplast precursors in the newly formed daughter merozoites
Finally there is partial but significant colocalization between MAL13P1.156 and the apicoplast marker EF-Tu

GeneSummary.bullet_point: Overexpression of MAL13P1.156 increases parasite resistance to ionomycin by approximately 2-fold (P value 0.01) at 0.5 μM ionomycin concentration, with survival rates comparable to parasites grown in medium supplemented with 500 μM CaCl2.
supporting_quotes: At 0.5 μM of ionomycin (that roughly corresponds to the ionomycin IC50; see below), the survival of the PfACBP1 overexpressing cell line is ~2-fold higher (P value 0.01) compared to the nontransfected parasites
The survival rate of the transgenic cell line is comparable to the nontransfected parasites grown in the medium supplemented with 500 μM of CaCl2

GeneSummary.bullet_point: The protein undergoes proteolytic processing upon import to the apicoplast, showing a full-length fusion protein of 91 kDa and a processed form of ~72 kDa, consistent with signal peptide cleavage.
supporting_quotes: Western blot analyses show a strong expression of this protein as a full-length fusion protein of 91 kDa (64 kDa full-length protein plus 27 kDa GFP) and a processed form ~72 kDa
This proteolytic cleavage is consistent with the signal peptide processing upon import to the apicoplast

GeneSummary.bullet_point: Among 545 plastid targeted proteins analyzed, MAL13P1.156 showed the highest homology to the EF-hand consensus sequence and shares structural similarity with calcium binding proteins from other organisms including Entamoeba histolytica, Cryptosporidium parvum, and Toxoplasma gondii.
supporting_quotes: In our bioinformatics analyses of the 545 plastid targeted proteins, PfACBP1 showed the highest homology to the EF-hand consensus sequence which suggests its crucial role in calcium-mediated regulatory function(s) in this compartment
Multiple alignments of the amino acids spanning the EF-hand domain (214th to 341th positions) show considerable conservation of the calcium binding domain between these structural homologues

AdditionalInferences: The protein likely functions as a calcium sensor and/or buffer in the apicoplast, similar to calcium binding proteins in plant chloroplasts
MAL13P1.156 may help retain higher calcium concentrations in the apicoplast through its calcium binding properties, protecting against calcium depletion
The protein represents a potential target for understanding calcium-dependent regulation of apicoplast gene expression
Given its role in calcium homeostasis, MAL13P1.156 could be explored as a potential drug target for liver stage malaria parasites
data.ShortSummary: MAL13P1.156 (PfACBP1) is an apicoplast-targeted calcium binding protein containing an EF-hand domain that increases parasite resistance to calcium ionophores and likely plays a crucial role in calcium homeostasis within the apicoplast organelle.

data.short_summary: ACBP1 is an acyl-CoA binding protein that binds long-chain acyl-CoA esters and localizes to the cytoplasm, playing a role in lipid metabolism in Plasmodium falciparum.

PDs.code_reason: Direct binding assays demonstrated specific binding to long-chain acyl-CoA esters
Contains conserved acyl-CoA binding domain identified through sequence analysis

RPD.code_reason: Direct experimental evidence including protein localization via immunofluorescence, Western blot analysis showing signal peptide processing, and functional assays demonstrating increased ionomycin resistance upon overexpression.
